intro: You are in Xanthos, an ancient city in Antalya province whose story goes back to the 8th century BC. It was Lycia's largest city and the capital of monumental tomb architecture.
history: Xanthos has a proud and painful past: twice in its history, the city chose self-immolation over surrender. It also gave us the richest collection of Lycian inscriptions known.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Harpy Monument and the Nereid Monument, the Lycian sarcophagi and the theatre, and finally the Letoon sanctuary.
facts: Did you know? Twice in its history the city burned itself rather than surrender: first to the Persians, then to Brutus in Rome's civil war. Herodotus and Appian each record one. In 1842 the Nereid and Harpy Monument reliefs were removed to the British Museum, where the original blocks of the Nereid Monument are displayed today; casts stand in their place here. And the inscribed pillar here carries the longest known text in Lycian, a key document in deciphering the language.
outro: This brings our tour of Xanthos to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
